data.title: Tansun Surges on News of Deal to Purchase 20,000 Nvidia GPUs
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 9 -- Chinese fintech service provider Tansun Technology has announced a deal involving procurement of 20,000 new RTX PRO 5500 Blackwell chips from US chip giant Nvidia. The chips are eagerly anticipated by the market and there has been much speculation about the pricing.

Tansun [SHE: 300872] closed up 12.38 percent at CNY16.16 (USD2.4) today, following the announcement, even though no further details about the deal were revealed. Yicai called the firm, posing as an investor, and a member of staff said they still need to confirm whether the disclosure requirements have been met.

The RTX PRO 5500 Blackwell is not typically regarded as a chip suitable for large-scale artificial intelligence training and inference in data centers, but rather as a workstation product. Nvidia’s website says the RTX PRO 5500 Blackwell Workstation Edition is "coming soon," indicating it has not yet been officially launched.

The RTX PRO series is a product line designed for professional-grade AI and graphics technology and it has 84 gigabytes of high-speed memory. The RTX PRO 5500 Blackwell Workstation Edition is designed for professionals in areas such as media and entertainment, architecture, engineering and healthcare. It is suitable for generative AI, physical AI applications and scientific computing and data analysis.

Although the RTX PRO 5500 Blackwell Workstation Edition can run AI workloads, it still falls significantly short compared to graphics processing units commonly used in AI data centers. In terms of memory bandwidth, which impacts AI performance, the RTX PRO 5500 Blackwell has a memory bandwidth of 1,395 GB per second. In contrast, Nvidia’s H100 data center GPU boasts a memory bandwidth of 3 terabytes per second.

Even though it has not yet been launched, the market is still keenly interested in the price of the product. Yicai found that on e-commerce platforms, the price for the 72GB RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell workstation edition is between CNY61,000 and CNY77,000 (USD9,115 and USD11,506), while the 96GB RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell workstation edition is priced between CNY123,000 and CNY146,000 (USD18,379 and USD21,816).

On this basis, the price of the RTX PRO 5500 Blackwell can be estimated at CNY80,000 to CNY120,000. This suggests that the total procurement amount for Tansun could be between CNY1.6 billion and CNY2.4 billion (USD239 million and USD358 million).

According to Tansun’s website, it serves clients in the financial industry, mainly banks, and it uses AI and blockchain technology to provide consulting, fintech products, and services.

The Beijing-based firm sees promising growth potential in its computing power leasing business, which offers long-term computing power services to leading internet ecosystems and large language model companies. In June this year, Tansun announced a partnership with Capitalonline Data Service to establish a joint venture focused on computing power leasing, with Tansun contributing CNY70 million (USD10.46 million) to the venture.

Last year, Tansun reported a revenue increase of 0.6 percent year-on-year, reaching CNY1.78 billion. However, having previously made a profit it slipped back into the red with a net loss of CNY138 million (USD20.62 million). The company attributed this to several factors, including intensified market competition, increased project management challenges, business transformation, and personnel restructuring.

Editor: Tom Litting

data.title: JAC Motors Shares Tumble as Brake Pedal Failures in Huawei-Backed Maextro V800 Raise Concerns
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 9 -- Shares of JAC Motors hit the daily limit down again today after a video showing brake pedal brackets breaking during tests of the Maextro V800, a luxury vehicle it jointly developed with Huawei Technologies, sparked safety concerns.

JAC Motors [SHA: 600418] hit the daily 10 percent decline limit for the second consecutive session before recovering to close 8 percent lower at CNY22.75 (USD3.40) per share.

The Hefei-based automaker jointly developed premium new energy vehicle brand Maextro with telecoms equipment giant Huawei under the latter's Harmony Intelligent Mobility Alliance. The Maextro V800, a large extended-range electric multi-purpose vehicle launched in August, targets the premium business market and is priced between CNY766,000 and CNY1 million (USD114,290 to USD151,590).

Automotive information platform Dongchedi, owned by ByteDance, recently released a video showing the brake pedal brackets of three Maextro V800 vehicles fracturing during tests measuring braking performance from 100 kilometers per hour to a complete stop, resulting in a loss of braking ability.

Responding to the video yesterday, Maextro said its braking systems had been developed and validated to standards exceeding national and industry requirements, and that no brake pedal bracket base fractures had occurred during actual use since deliveries began.

“User safety is always our top priority," Maextro said. "Even in non-standard extreme testing conditions, we still hope to provide users with higher security redundancy: we will further optimize the design of this component and provide free upgrade options for users.”

The company added that it would systematically review and strengthen the design validation, testing parameters, and production quality management of the relevant components.

Brake Testing Methods Under Scrutiny

Dongchedi disputed Maextro's characterization of the tests as extreme. A representative of the platform said braking tests from 100 kilometers per hour to a complete stop are among the most basic vehicle performance assessments, the National Business Daily reported.

Dongchedi said this was the first time it had encountered a brake pedal bracket fracture during such testing, with similar fractures occurring at the same location in three consecutive tests.

Addressing questions about the force applied to the brake pedal during the tests, Dongchedi said the actual peak force was 1,612 newtons, equivalent to the weight of about 164 kilograms and substantially more than drivers typically apply during routine braking.

The dispute has also raised questions about how much force a brake pedal should withstand. No unified industry standard specifies the maximum force a driver can apply to a brake pedal, according to Qiu Jincao, deputy secretary-general of the Automotive Advanced Power Systems Branch of the China Society of Automotive Engineers.

“Under normal driver operation, the brake pedal should not break, regardless of the circumstances,” Qiu said. He added that automakers establish their own internal standards based on vehicle structures and safety redundancy requirements.

Other experts noted that the direction of force applied to the brake pedal, testing methods, and ultimate load data could all affect the results. The precise cause of the fractures has yet to be determined and requires further verification.

As of publication, Yicai found that the video was no longer available for viewing on several platforms, including Bilibili, WeChat Channels, RedNote and Douyin.

Editor: Emmi Laine

data.title: Chinese Firms Build Regional Value Chains in Southeast Asia, OCBC China President Says
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 9 -- Chinese companies are moving beyond simply setting up factories in Southeast Asia to build integrated regional value chains, tap local consumer markets and deepen their local presence, the president of Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp.’s China division told Yicai at the recent FutureChina Global Forum 2026.

In the early stages of their expansion into Southeast Asia, Chinese firms often simply relocated their production bases from China to the region, said Wang Ke, who is also chief executive officer of the Singaporean bank’s Hong Kong operations.

However, they are now increasingly leveraging the different strengths of individual Southeast Asian markets to distribute sourcing, manufacturing, distribution and service operations across the region, while maintaining links with China to form integrated regional value chains, he said.

The electric vehicle industry offers a good example, Wang said. Chinese companies may manufacture batteries in Indonesia to take advantage of its resource base, produce chips for smart cockpits in Malaysia and carry out final vehicle assembly in Thailand.

Beyond serving as a manufacturing base, Southeast Asia is also becoming an increasingly important consumer market for Chinese firms expanding overseas, Wang said. In this respect, Chinese companies are following a similar path to that taken by multinational corporations when they entered China 20 or even 25 years ago.

Chinese firms are no longer simply expanding overseas, they are increasingly seeking to establish local roots. To achieve long-term growth in foreign markets, businesses need to integrate into local economies by developing local suppliers, creating skilled jobs, engaging with local communities and building their brands in those markets. Some Chinese companies have already begun to embark on this path, he added.

Cross-Border Financial Services

As a result of this regional layout, Chinese firms’ demand for financial services with both regional reach and local expertise is increasing, Wang said. Financial institutions must not only provide strong services in individual markets but also maintain a regional presence that enables them to support cross-border financing, cash management and risk management.

Singapore is a major hub for financing services in Southeast Asia. For example, projects in Indonesia may require funding beyond what the local financial market can readily provide, given constraints on the availability of certain foreign currencies. Companies may therefore opt to secure financing in Singapore to fund procurement and construction for projects in Indonesia, creating a new demand for cross-border financing.

Businesses’ financial needs also extend beyond securing funding. They may face issues such as currency mismatches when borrowing in US dollars but making payments in Indonesia in the local currency, exposing them to foreign-exchange and interest-rate risks. They must also consider the timing of financing and whether interest-rate hedging is necessary, Wang said.

AI as Growth Driver

Wang also highlighted artificial intelligence as an increasingly important driver of global economic growth. Southeast Asia is an attractive market for Chinese technology and AI firms thanks to its young population, high levels of digital literacy and strong receptiveness to technology-driven business models.

High-tech and AI businesses are inherently regional in nature, Wang said. Although Southeast Asia consists of 10 separate national markets, these firms can expand across borders relatively smoothly. Their investments also generate demand beyond technology itself, driving the need for supporting infrastructure, including data centers, cloud services and energy facilities.

Looking ahead, Southeast Asia could see growing demand for cross-regional energy collaboration. For instance, Malaysia and Thailand are well-suited for solar power generation, while Vietnam is ideal for wind energy. The green electricity generated in these countries could eventually be transmitted via smart grids to high-demand areas such as Singapore and Indonesia.

Chinese companies possess the technology and experience required and are well positioned to participate in and support the development of green infrastructure across Southeast Asia, he added.

Editor: Kim Taylor

data.title: China’s Geely, Nio Strengthen Battery-Swap Alliance With Cross-Shareholding Deal
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 28 -- Chinese automotive giant Geely Holding Group and electric vehicle manufacturer Nio will deepen their strategic cooperation on battery swapping and EV charging through a cross-shareholding arrangement at the subsidiary level, aimed at accelerating the expansion of their battery-swap and charging service networks.

Geely will use its 100 percent equity in its battery-swap service provider Yiyi Internet Technology and CNY640 million (USD95.3 million) in cash to subscribe to newly issued shares in Nio’s battery-swap and charging unit Nio Power, Shanghai-based Nio said today. Upon completion of the transaction, Geely will hold a 30 percent stake in Nio Power, which will have a post-investment valuation of CNY16 billion (USD2.4 billion).

Nio was one of the earliest Chinese EV manufacturers to adopt battery swapping and set up Nio Power in 2017 to develop and run a battery-swap and charging service network. As of Sept. 20, Nio operated 4,099 battery-swap stations and 5,289 charging stations, and had provided users with over 120 million battery swaps in total, it said.

Yiyi, founded in 2017, managed more than 470 battery-swap stations in over 40 cities across China as of April last year, and has plans to expand to 2,000 stations by next year, according to its website.

The integration of Yiyi into Nio Power will accelerate the expansion of Nio's battery swapping network, with the aim of building 10,000 battery-swap stations by 2030, Nio said. The two sides will also work together to establish unified battery-swapping technology standards, while Hangzhou-based Geely will develop battery-swap vehicles models for consumers.

Nio will also acquire a stake in Geely’s EV charging service provider Zhejiang Haohan Energy Technology, according to the agreement between the two parties. Upon completion of the transaction, Nio will hold a 10 percent stake in Haohan, and both sides will share resources to expand charging network coverage and improve operational efficiency.

Haohan currently operates 2,500 charging stations and 12,000 charging guns in 232 cities across China. By the end of 2027, it plans to expand its network to 22,000 charging stations and 100,000 charging guns, Geely said.

The collaboration between Nio and Geely dates back to November 2023, when Nio announced plans to form a battery swapping alliance with automakers. Since then, it has established partnerships with eight automakers, including Changan Automobile and Geely.

Editor: Kim Taylor

data.title: Chinese Developer Greentown Slides as Ex-Chairman Charged in USD2.5 Million Bribery Case
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 9 -- Shares in Greentown China Holdings slumped today after Hong Kong’s anti-corruption body charged the Chinese property developer’s former board chairman with allegedly accepting HKD20 million (USD2.5 million) in bribes in connection with the acquisition of a stake in a real estate firm.

Greentown’s share price [HKG: 3900] closed down 3.6 percent at HKD6.14 (USD0.75). The stock has lost 28 percent of its value so far this year.

Zhang Yudong, who stepped down in March last year due to work arrangements, allegedly conspired with several people, including a shareholder of a Dalian-based real estate firm, to accept bribes of HKD20 million between January 2020 and March 2023, the Independent Commission Against Corruption said today. The alleged arrangement enabled Hangzhou-based Greentown to acquire an equity stake in the property developer.

Zhang has been charged with one count of conspiracy for an agent to accept an advantage, in violation of Section 9(1)(a) of the Prevention of Bribery Ordinance and Section 159A of the Crimes Ordinance, the ICAC said. The case is scheduled to be brought before the Eastern Magistrates’ Courts today.

Zhang joined Greentown as chief executive officer in May 2018 and succeeded the company’s founder, Song Weiping, as chairman of the board in July 2019. Before that, the 58-year-old served as deputy mayor of Dalian in northeastern Liaoning province, overseeing urban construction and management.

The charges follow an earlier announcement by Greentown that the ICAC had executed a search warrant at the company’s main office in Hong Kong on June 17. The firm said the probe concerned corruption allegations involving an independent individual who had previously served as a director, sparking market speculation about the case. The ICAC announcement has now shed light on the matter.

Founded in 1995 as a private real estate developer, Greentown became a state-controlled company in 2014 when China Communications Construction Group, a state-owned infrastructure giant, acquired a stake in the business. The group held approximately 29 percent of Greentown as of June 30.

Greentown has come under pressure from the downturn in China’s property market. Its net profit plunged 61 percent in the first half from a year earlier to CNY81.7 million (USD12.2 million), while revenue sank 26 percent to CNY39.5 billion (USD5.9 billion), according to the firm’s latest financial report.

Editors: Dou Shicong, Kim Taylor

data.title: China's Kengic Wins USD11.2 Million Bid for Polish E-Commerce Logistics Hub
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 9 -- Chinese logistics solutions provider Kengic Intelligent Technology has won a CNY75 million (USD11.2 million) bid to build an automated warehousing system in Poland for a major global e-commerce firm.

The project involves supporting infrastructure for an overseas warehousing hub operated by a globally renowned cross-border e-commerce company, the Qingdao-based firm announced yesterday. Kengic did not disclose the identity of the project owner or further details, citing commercial confidentiality.

Kengic is finalizing a contract with the project tenderer, with the CNY75 million tax-inclusive bid subject to the final agreement. The timing of the contract signing and execution remains uncertain, the firm said, adding that the project should boost earnings if successfully completed.

Founded in 2015, Kengic provides automated logistics and manufacturing systems for industries including chemicals, automotive and energy storage. The firm has completed more than 1,000 projects in 17 countries, according to its website.

The new partnership failed to boost the company's shares as Kengic [SHA: 688455] closed 0.9 percent down at CNY17.17 (USD2.60) today.

Editor: Emmi Laine

data.title: China’s Longpan Technology Pares Gains After Initial Rally on Geely Battery Unit Supply Deal
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 9 -- Longpan Technology’s shares trimmed a large early gain made after the leading Chinese producer of lithium iron phosphate cathode materials announced a major five-year order from a unit of automotive giant Geely Holding Group that could generate sales of as much as CNY25.6 billion (USD3.82 billion).

After climbing by almost 9 percent in Shanghai this morning, Longpan Technology [SHA: 603906] walked back most of that increase to close up 0.6 percent at CNY21.07 (USD3.15) per share.

Nanjing Liyuan Nano Technology, an indirectly held subsidiary of Longpan Technology, has signed an agreement with Zhejiang Jiyao Tongxing Energy Technology to supply it with 378,600 to 567,800 tons of LFP cathode materials between 2026 and 2030, its Nanjing-based parent company announced late yesterday. Actual volume will be determined by subsequent purchase orders, it said.

Longpan Technology added that apart from this agreement, it was not aware of any other recent material developments that could explain significant moves in the company’s share price. Prior to today, the stock had risen by its 10-percent daily trading limit for two straight trading sessions.

The company did not estimate the value of the order, noting only that product prices would be confirmed monthly based on agreed terms. If supply-and-demand conditions in the new energy and advanced materials markets change significantly during the period, the two parties will renegotiate prices, it said. The firm did not reveal any further details of the project.

Using an estimated average selling price of CNY45,023 (USD6,722) per metric ton -- calculated based on LFP cathode material sales revenue and volume disclosed in Longpan’s most recent earnings report -- the upper end of the agreed supply volume could generate about CNY25.6 billion in sales.

Lopal Technology said the agreement and its implementation would help establish a long-term, stable relationship with a downstream customer, strengthen its competitiveness in new energy battery materials and have a positive impact on its future business performance.

Jiyao Tongxing Energy is a battery unit of privately held Geely. Its products are used primarily in new energy vehicles within the Geely group. In May last year, the company announced a strategic target of reaching 70 gigawatt hours of annual battery production capacity by next year, covering both power packs for vehicles and energy storage systems.

In the first eight months of this year, Jiyao Tongxing Energy’s cumulative installed power battery capacity in vehicles reached 11.7 GWh, according to figures from the China Automotive Power Battery Industry Innovation Alliance. It had a 2.4 percent share of the domestic market, ranking ninth among battery manufacturers in China.

Editor: Tom Litting

data.title: Long-Distance Travel, Smaller-City Tourism Gain Ground Over China’s ‘Golden Week’ Holiday
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 9 -- Long-distance travel, tourism in smaller cities, inbound tourism, and artificial intelligence-enhanced cultural and tourism consumption emerged as new aspects of the holiday economy over China’s recent “Golden Week” break.

Some 2.14 billion cross-regional passenger trips were made in China over the National Day holiday from Oct. 1 to 7, up 0.6 percent from a year ago to average 306 million a day, according to the Ministry of Transport. That helped to unlock consumer spending potential and boost both online and offline consumption, said Gao Bo, deputy head of the ministry’s transport services department.

Tourist spending increased 4.3 percent to CNY738.3 billion (USD110 billion) in the period from a year earlier, the Ministry of Culture and Tourism announced today.

Robust travel demand shows that consumers are not necessarily unwilling to spend, said Luo Zhiheng, chief economist at Yuekai Securities, adding that the key question is how to convert that demand more fully and sustainably into consumption.

Expanding and upgrading cultural and tourism consumption will require refinements to institutional arrangements to address three main obstacles: ensuring people have time to travel, offering destinations and products that are worth visiting, and maintaining a trustworthy, well-regulated market, Luo said.

Self-driving remained the dominant means of travel during the so-called “Golden Week” break. Road passenger trips hit 1.96 billion, with self-driven journeys accounting for nearly 80 percent. Traffic levels involving new energy vehicles jumped 35 percent from a year ago, while rail and air traffic also remained at high levels.

Value-added tax invoice data showed that average daily sales across China’s service consumption-related industries climbed almost 20 percent year on year. Revenue from sightseeing and entertainment services, cultural and artistic services, and sports services rose about 24 percent, 21 percent, and 29 percent, respectively.

Extended Break

The relatively short three-day interval between the Mid-Autumn Festival and National Day holidays boosted interest in long-distance travel. The average one-way distance for domestic travel over the break increased to about 560 kilometers, according to data from online travel agency Trip.Com.

Bookings for destinations such as Xizang Autonomous Region and Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region as well as the provinces of Guizhou and Qinghai rose significantly, Trip.Com’s figures showed, while air ticket sales on routes over 2,000 kilometers increased by more than 40 percent.

Tourism in smaller cities also gained traction. Visits to leisure and entertainment venues in third-tier and lower-tier cities more than tripled from the pre-holiday period, outpacing the growth rate in first- and second-tier cities, according to data from Meituan and Dianping, major local-life service platforms. Nanchang, Zhongshan, and Yangzhou were among the popular destinations.

Inbound tourism expanded further during the holiday. Foreign nationals made 682,000 entries into China, including 505,000 under visa-waiver policies, with the two numbers rising 5.4 percent and 9.2 percent, respectively. Cities and regions across China have been improving services for international visitors, including payment options, ticket booking, and itinerary planning, to make travel more convenient.

Meanwhile, AI is becoming more deeply integrated into cultural and tourism consumption. Meituan said searches for its AI concierge Xiaotuan climbed 29 percent over the holiday compared with the preceding period, as users sought information about local businesses. Demand for smart products also picked up, with sales of embodied AI robots, smart glasses, and similar products seeing rapid year-on-year growth.

Editor: Tom Litting

data.title: [Exclusive] ANTA Group’s Chairman Ding on the Multi-Brand Strategy Behind the PUMA Deal
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 8 – The Board Chairman of ANTA Sports Products Limited ("ANTA Group" or the “Group”), Ding Shizhong, shared his views on the Chinese sporting-goods giant’s “single-focus, multi-brand, globalization” strategy, its approach to managing a multi brand portfolio and his phased approach to business during a recent in-depth two-and-a-half-hour conversation with Yicai in Xiamen.

Just a few days after the interview, ANTA Group announced that it had completed its acquisition of a 29.06 percent stake in PUMA SE for EUR1.5055 billion (USD1.6 billion) in cash, officially becoming the German sportswear company’s largest shareholder.

“We don’t want to be China's Nike, we want to be the world's ANTA,” said Ding, who was dressed in an ANTA Guanjun T-shirt and a KOLON SPORT jacket, paired with Salomon shoes.

Ding first set out this vision in 2005. Over 20 years later, he repeatedly stressed during the interview that simply replicating the business models of already successful international brands and trying to surpass them would be almost impossible. ANTA Group therefore had to find a different path.

This led to its "single focus, multi-brand, globalization" strategy. From FILA and Descente to Amer Sports and Jack Wolfskin, more than a dozen brands have been brought into ANTA Group’s business portfolio through different forms of investment and acquisition.

ANTA Group has evolved from a single-brand company with annual revenue of just over CNY5 billion (USD746 million) in 2009, when it acquired FILA, into an international multi-brand sportswear group. Including Amer Sports, in which ANTA Group is the largest shareholder, these two companies’ annual revenue now exceeds CNY120 billion (USD17.9 billion), while ANTA Group’s market capitalization is above HKD200 billion (USD25.5 billion).

Responding to criticism that ANTA Group has relied on acquisitions to drive its growth, Ding told Yicai that “ANTA is not in the business of buying and selling brands for financial gains. We are committed to building and operating businesses for the long term.”

The key test, he said, is whether an acquired brand can create value for consumers and whether its products continue to improve after the acquisition. Ding described himself as a long-term thinker. Investing in the Herzogenaurach-based PUMA had actually been under internal consideration for a decade but never materialized because the conditions aren't ripe yet.

He compared the acquisition process to sailing a ship. The captain must remain committed to the destination while continuously adjusting the ship's course according to the weather, wind direction, waves and condition of the crew. This is what Ding calls his "phased approach."

Why PUMA?

PUMA’s assets, product portfolio, sports expertise and global value chain are highly complementary to ANTA Group’s, Ding said. "ANTA does not have a strong presence in football, while PUMA excels in that area,” he said. “PUMA also has a strong lineup in motorsport equipment as well as advanced technologies in running and professional track and field."

ANTA Group will participate in PUMA’s governance at the supervisory-board level, while "respecting PUMA's brand DNA and maintaining its independence," Ding said.

Management Model

How does ANTA Group manage a diverse portfolio of brands? Ding described the group serves as an enabler for its multiple brands.  The better a brand performs, the less intervention by the group is needed. The group only steps in when a brand encounters problems and requires support.

At the group level, ANTA focuses on strategic alignment, risk management and shared back-office capabilities. It provides brands with services ranging from supply chain management and logistics to IT and talent development and risk management, but it does not interfere in their day-to-day operations.

"Our multi-brand management model currently has no direct equivalent anywhere in the world,” Ding said. “We have developed it through our own hands-on experience."

Ding believes that any sports brand without professional performance capabilities and specialized technology cannot truly be considered a sports brand. He said brand value should be judged on four criteria, namely technical expertise, product functionality in real-world sporting scenarios, reliable quality and accumulated brand heritage and culture.

“Simply copying someone else’s successful model is unlikely to help you surpass them. Both the ANTA Group and its individual brands must find their own path to success. Building a brand takes time, and taking a brand global is, in essence, about bringing its culture to the world. For ANTA, this means not only introducing our brand identity and culture to the global consumers, but also demonstrating that Chinese companies have the capabilities to successfully manage global brands."

However, focusing exclusively on professional athletes and enthusiasts can limit the brand’s growth potential. The goal, he said, is to make top-notch professional technology accessible to everyone."

Ding pointed to the Salomon XT6 city commuting shoes he was wearing as an example. The product removes waterproofing that most consumers do not need in everyday use while retaining other advanced technologies. Since ANTA Group acquired Amer Sports that is home to Arc'teryx in 2019, the scale of Arc'teryx’s professional products has doubled.

Group Anchor

In Ding's view, ANTA's flagship brand remains the "anchor" of the group, with retail sales exceeding CNY45 billion (USD6.7 billion) last year. Its strategy going forward includes maintaining its positioning in mass-market sports, leveraging global resources to enter more markets, increasing investment in research and development as well as continuing to support Chinese sports.

Over the past decade, ANTA Group has invested over CNY20 billion (USD2.9 billion) in research and development. In 2005, it established the sports industry's first sports science laboratory. It is now investing several billion Chinese yuan, equivalent to hundreds of millions of US dollars, to build the Group’s Global Innovation Industrial Park.

Ding believes the ultimate competition among sports brands is not about traffic, distribution channels or mergers and acquisitions, but rather about innovations in sports science, product technology, and performance-driven design.

At the recent 20th Asian Games Aichi-Nagoya, 43 percent of the 169 gold medals won by the Chinese delegation came from athletes representing the 20 national teams sponsored by ANTA.

Brand Globalization

On international expansion, Ding distinguishes between corporate globalization and brand globalization. The former, he said, means developing management capabilities on a global scale, while the latter means building connections with consumers in markets around the world.

"ANTA Group's path is to drive brand globalization through corporate globalization, leveraging the capabilities developed through its multi-brand portfolio to support the main brand. The ultimate goal is for ANTA, a brand that grew out of China, to become a brand respected by global consumers," Ding said.

Looking back on more than 30 years in the business, Ding recalled that he travelled into Beijing at the age of 17 with 600 pairs of shoes. Reflecting on his “phased approach” to business, he cited a belief that has guided his entrepreneurial journey. "Many successful people in this world are not necessarily better at what they do than you are. They simply dare to do more."

Ding said that ANTA Group today is already "highly internationalized" in terms of its governance structure, shareholder composition, organizational capabilities and market footprint. In that sense, he said, it has become "the world's ANTA."

The next step is to become a company that is "respected," in other words, respected by consumers and around the world. "We will adhere to long-term thinking and unconditional optimism, stay rooted in the real economy, maintain a consumer-oriented approach and strive to become a company respected by people around the world," Ding said.

"I believe that as a company grows, its corporate culture is shaped by the core values and beliefs espoused by its founder. ANTA Group has grown a small business into an industry leader with a growing global presence. Along this journey, we have come to recognize that building a successful company is about more than just financial performance.  It is equally important to reflect on the broader value we create as a business." He said.

“As ANTA has grown, we have remained committed to giving back to society. I have often asked myself, 'As a public company, what more can we do for our employees and for society?' Today, we provide our employees with competitive compensation and benefits, while continuing to invest in philanthropic indicatives that create lasting value for the communities we serve.”

“ANTA Group has contributed nearly CNY2 billion to support sports and healthy lifestyles among young people in underdeveloped regions, benefiting over 10 million children and adolescents. Over the past three years, we have also partnered with the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) to provide humanitarian assistance to more than 300,000 displaced young people.”

He further stated, "Our family has established the Hemin Foundation with an endowment of CNY10 billion. Through the foundation, we have committed CNY2 billion to building a public hospital in Jinjiang, in partnership with the Shanghai Sixth People’s Hospital.  The hospital will serve as a national regional medical center."

Editor: Kim Taylor

data.title: Far Greater Priority Should be Given to AI Security, Insider Says
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 29 -- The capabilities of artificial intelligence models are growing at a frightening pace but global investment in developing the security systems needed to keep AI under control is far from adequate, an industry expert has warned.

“Rather than expanding the boundaries of model capabilities, we should focus more energy and resources on testing the reliability and security of models. This is what we should start doing today,” Zhang Hongjiang, an investment partner at Chinese venture capital firm Source Code Capital and an expert in the computer field, said in an interview with Yicai during the recent FutureChina Global Forum in Singapore.

Zhang has a strong industry background, having served as chief technology officer for Microsoft Asia-Pacific Research and Development Group and chief executive officer of Kingsoft Corporation. He also founded the Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence in 2018 and still serves as its founding chairman.

AI Security Risks Are Growing

In July, a cutting-edge agent model from US firm OpenAI "escaped" during testing. It bypassed the isolated sandbox constraints and hacked the open-source platform Hugging Face, signaling that AI may have crossed some red lines, Zhang said.

“For me, this is a very important event, not because of how much harm it has caused, but because this model was designed without malicious intent,” Zhang stated, adding this is even more concerning because “it has the ability to design its own behaviors without realizing the risks involved.”

AI models are now capable of achieving gold-medal results in the International Mathematical Olympiad, meaning that a general-purpose model without specialized training can outperform most professionals on specialized problems, Zhang pointed out.

"When an AI’s IQ exceeds 140 and it is backed by a powerful knowledge base, its capabilities become immense, and that is a frightening prospect," he noted.

Safety More Important Than Competition

AI is entering a highly competitive stage, and countries and companies are competing to launch ever more advanced models. In this context, we cannot rely on individual countries or institutions to “self-restrain,” Zhang said, and we must establish cross-border coordination and supervision mechanisms that prioritize security.

Zhang mentioned nuclear safety as an example. In order to prevent disasters like the Chernobyl nuclear power plant accident from happening again, the majority of research funding for nuclear power plants is now dedicated to safety. But controlling AI is more difficult than nuclear power regulation, he warned.

Nuclear tests and facilities leave physical traces that can be verified through multiple sources such as satellite imagery and seismic monitoring, but the form of AI models is software, which makes tracking more difficult.

Also, nuclear testing is mostly in the hands of a limited number of national institutions, while AI models are being developed by companies all over the world whose priority is commercial success and strong market positions, making security more complicated, Zhang explained.

While it is true that if one nation pauses its progress, another may catch up, a "zero-sum" mindset is inappropriate for AI, given how profound and wide-ranging its influence will be in society. "National interests must yield in the face of risks to humanity's future survival," Zhang said.

Editors: Dou Shicong, Tom Litting

data.title: Unveiling the "Molecular Scissors" and Life Switches of Cells: An Interview with 2026 WLF Prize Laureate in Life Science or Medicine Dr. Vishva DIXIT
data.description:
Yicai) Oct. 9 -- Background Introduction: In the grand landscape of biomedicine, deciphering how cells "actively choose to die" represents a profound revolution in understanding biological development and human disease. Dr. Vishva DIXIT has been awarded the 2026 World Laureates Foundation Prize in Life Science or Medicine for his historic contributions to the molecular mechanisms of cell death and inflammation. During his medical studies at the University of Nairobi, he resolved to devote himself to basic biomedical research. After moving to the US, Dr. DIXIT completed pathology training at Washington University in St. Louis and subsequently launched his research career at the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor and Genentech.

1. Sickness Transcends National Boundaries: Collaborate for Humanity

Q：How do you feel about receiving the 2026 WLF Prize in Life Science or Medicine?

Dr. Vishva DIXIT: I was very surprised and deeply honored to share this award with good friends and admired pioneers—WANG Xiaodong, YUAN Junying, and SHAO Feng.

My message to the global audience is that sickness transcends any national boundary. A sick person does not care where a medicine was discovered. We must work together as global collaborators for humanity.

2. “The Executioner is Like a Set of Molecular Scissors, Irreversibly Cutting Up Crucial Proteins”

Q：Your work played a historic role in revealing how cells actively choose to die. If you were to explain your discovery to a non-biologist using a simple everyday analogy, what kind of "internal shutdown switch" did you uncover to help the body clear out damaged cells?

Dr. Vishva DIXIT: Yeah, it's a great question. We live because we die in a sense that injured cells, mutant cells, old cells all have to die so that new cells, younger cells can replace them. But the question becomes then, how does a cell decide to die? And if it decides to die, what is the nature of the executioner? In the real world, if somebody is killed, we would ask, are they shot, were they stabbed? How did they die? And the process of cell death is important, not only for diseased cells and old cells and mutant cells, but also in development when we are being formed as embryos, it is involved in the sculpting of the human form so that orifices like your mouth are created by cells deciding to die.

So that raises a very important question: what is the arbitrator, who is the judge that says "you must die, you must live"? And then what is the nature of the executioner? Our work really illuminated that the executioner is a set of molecular scissors. It's like a scissors that cuts up the inside of a cell, cuts up crucial proteins, components of the cell. And because of this cutting, which is irreversible, once you cut, you can't rejoin, then the cell dies. But this executioner apparatus, these molecular scissors, are then governed by another structure, the arbitrators or judges—some are death receptors on the cell, in other cases molecules released from damaged mitochondria—and balanced by a whole family of molecules that inhibit cell death. Our study over the years has defined the executioners and how they are regulated by the inhibitors.

3. “The Biggest Bottleneck Was Overcoming Redundancy and Plasticity in Death Pathways”

Q: When cells get damaged, they need to safely clear themselves out like a bomb defusal team. But if this shutdown process gets out of control, it can trigger severe inflammation and autoimmune diseases. What was the most challenging bottleneck in mapping these molecular pathways, and how does your research help us stop this "friendly fire"?

Dr. Vishva DIXIT: I think the challenge was, to a certain extent, redundancy. By that, I mean if you block one death pathway, then another can take over. So there are many death pathways; you block one, another one takes over, and the cell still dies. And we had to do very complicated genetics to understand what you would think of as plasticity, that you inhibit something and another thing takes over, which made defining the components a challenge.

But now that the key components have been defined, we know the major players, it's an opportunity to pharmacologically manipulate them. So for the molecular scissors, for example, we could develop chemical inhibitors, opening up that possibility in drug development. So the bottleneck was overcoming this redundancy and mapping the pathways genetically.

4. “The Greatest Barrier in the 'Valley of Death' Is Safety Signals and Matching the Right Indication”

Q：You have spent decades at Genentech, one of the world's leading biotech companies. Many major scientific discoveries in the lab never make it into hospital medicine. As someone who understands both basic science and drug development, what is the hardest step in turning a fundamental biological discovery into a drug that saves real lives?

Dr. Vishva DIXIT: A very important component is patience. People don't realize how long it takes to go from a basic discovery to a drug. Everybody's excited about GLP-1 agonists, but work on them actually started in 1984. You have to be patient, focused, and persistent.

The valley of death in drug development is mostly safety signals. It is still very difficult to predict the safety of a medicine in humans, and many small molecules that work in animal models fail in humans because safety risks outweigh benefits. Another major reason drugs die is picking the wrong indication due to complex biology. Anti-TNF antibodies for inflammatory diseases—originally started off as a failure because they were developed for cancer. Matching the medicine to the right disease indication is critical.

5. “From BCL-2 Inhibitors in Leukemia to NLRP3 Targeted Therapies for Cardiovascular Disease”

Q：Which diseases do you think are now closest to benefiting from drugs that precisely manipulate cell-death or inflammatory pathways?

Dr. Vishva DIXIT: In cell death manipulation, the prime example is the BCL-2 inhibitor Venetoclax, used to treat chronic lymphocytic leukemia by overriding the death inhibitor BCL-2 in cancer cells that alter the life-death equilibrium to favor cell death.

In inflammation, the best example today is NLRP3 inhibitors. Phase 2 clinical trials by Eli Lilly and Nodthera in cardiovascular disease showed strong promise for patients with an inflammatory endotype marked by high C-reactive protein. If Phase 3 succeeds, it will change the complexion of cardiovascular treatment.

6. “The Question Should Not Be How Many Papers You Published, But What You Discovered”

Q：Biological experiments often involve repeated failures and uncertainty. What advice would you give to early-career researchers who spend months or even years on an experiment without getting the expected results?

Dr. Vishva DIXIT: Research is a difficult career because most of what you do fails. You have to be really passionate about it and driven by curiosity. Too often people are driven by getting a paper in Cell, Science, or Nature. I think the question should not be how many papers you have published, but what have you discovered?

If you are really passionate about research, understand that it's a long but very rewarding road, like being an explorer discovering things no one has seen before. Nature does not give up its secrets easily, so don't be attracted by just producing papers, but try to make a big discovery.

7. “Are We Alone in the Universe, or Is There Life Elsewhere?”

Q：As part of our "Science Relay," if you were to leave an open scientific guess or unsolved question for another award winner to answer, what would you ask them?

Dr. Vishva DIXIT: Now that we've discovered planets outside of our solar system and many galaxies, the question looms large whether there's life on those planets. With more sophisticated astrophysical instrumentation, the question I would put down is: Are we alone in the universe, or is there life elsewhere?

Prize Introduction

The World Laureates Foundation Prize (WLF Prize) is initiated and organized by the World Laureates Foundation, with exclusive prize funding donated by Sequoia China and support provided by Shanghai Lingang Science and Technology Innovation Development Foundation. The prize recognizes and supports outstanding researchers and technology pioneers worldwide for their contributions to science, selects and backs the world’s most promising young scholars, and creates a dual-award framework for dialogue, collaboration and joint development between top scientists and rising young scientific talents. It aims to advance global scientific and technological progress and inject new momentum into Shanghai’s efforts to build a world-class international science and innovation center with high quality.

The prize comprises three sub-awards: the World Laureates Foundation Prize in Computer Science or Mathematics (CSM), the World Laureates Foundation Prize in Life Science or Medicine (LSM), and the WLF Prize for Young Scientists.

data.title: Allist Slumps After Star Lung Cancer Drug Fails in Overseas Clinical Trial
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 8 -- Shares of Chinese innovative drug maker Allist Pharmaceuticals plummeted by the daily limit today, following disappointing results in an overseas Phase III clinical trial for its flagship product, lung cancer treatment Firmonertinib.

Allist [SHA: 688578] closed down 20 percent at CNY89.26 (USD13.32) today, cutting its market capitalization to CNY40.2 billion (USD6 billion). Firmonertinib accounts for nearly 99 percent of the Shanghai-based firm’s revenue.

The trial was co-conducted with the company’s US partner ArriVent BioPharma, which in 2021 acquired the rights to develop the drug outside China. The trial failed to show that Firmonertinib offered a meaningful delay in disease progression compared with standard chemotherapy, the firms revealed yesterday. 

The two partners said they are now evaluating the complete dataset from the trial to determine their follow-up plan. Pennsylvania-headquartered ArriVent announced the failure a day earlier than Allist, as markets were closed in China for the National Day holiday. ArriVent [NASDAQ: AVBP] slumped 47 percent on the news on Oct. 6, but rebounded 11.9 percent to USD16.89 yesterday.

Firmonertinib is a small molecule targeted drug used to treat non-small cell lung cancer caused by epidermal growth factor receptor mutations. The drug was approved for the market in China in March 2021 and quickly became a mainstream lung cancer treatment drug in the country. Last year, its sales reached CNY5.1 billion (USD761 million), accounting for 98.7 percent of Allist’s total revenue for 2025.

In order to expand overseas, Allist reached a cooperation agreement with ArriVent in July 2021, granting it the rights to develop and sell Firmonertinib in markets outside China. The deal gave Allist a down payment of USD40 million and potential future earnings of up to USD765 million as well as a stake in ArriVent.

The trial is one of two conducted for Firmonertinib by the two firms, and it enrolled 398 patients worldwide, with research centers in the US, Europe, Japan, and China.

The other international multicenter clinical trial targeting EGFR PACC mutations has also entered Phase III, with the first patient enrolled in December last year. EGFR PACC mutation is a rare subtype of EGFR mutations, accounting for about 12 percent of NSCLC patients who have EGFR mutations. As yet, there are no approved targeted drugs for it globally.

Editors: Dou Shicong, Tom Litting

data.title: Huawei, Qualcomm Ink Multi-Year Patent Deal Covering 5G, AI
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 8 -- Chinese tech giant Huawei Technologies and US chipmaker Qualcomm have signed a multi-year, broad patent license agreement that includes cross-licensing of their respective patent portfolios covering technologies such as fifth-generation wireless technology, computing, artificial intelligence and networking, the companies said on Oct. 5.

The agreement includes cross-licenses to the companies’ patent portfolios, while Qualcomm will also purchase certain US patents from Shenzhen-based Huawei covering computing, AI, networking and other technologies, Qualcomm said.

The transaction is subject to necessary regulatory approvals. The financial terms of the agreement were not disclosed.

Qualcomm also said assertions that the agreement was related to Huawei's chip architecture LogicFolding were not accurate. Separately, San Diego-based Qualcomm has agreed to purchase certain Huawei non-cellular US patents across multiple technology areas.

The agreement reflects the firms’ commitment to intellectual property rights and licensing practices consistent with fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory, or FRAND, principles, Qualcomm said.

The agreement recognizes Huawei’s continued innovation and intellectual property in 5G and other technology fields, said John Han, executive vice president and general manager of Qualcomm Technology Licensing.

The deal demonstrates the value of Huawei’s innovations and recognizes Qualcomm’s contributions to modern communication technologies, said Huawei Chief Intellectual Property Officer Alan Fan.

Chinese brokerages see opportunities in domestic AI computing and optical interconnects as Huawei accelerates its AI infrastructure development. China International Capital Corp. said the company’s faster Ascend chip rollout could boost domestic computing investment, while TF Securities expects its NPO-based SuperPoD to drive demand for optical components.

Editor: Kim Taylor

data.title: China Targets Launch of World's First Equatorial Deep-Sea Neutrino Telescope in 2027
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 8 -- China aims to bring the world’s first deep-sea neutrino telescope near the equator into operation next year, following successful prototype testing in the South China Sea, as part of a broader international effort to use neutrinos to investigate some of the least understood phenomena in the universe.

TRIDENT, short for Tropical Deep-sea Neutrino Telescope, will be deployed near the equator in 2027, Xu Donglian, the project’s initiator and chief scientist, told Yicai in a recent interview. “We’ve completed comprehensive validation of the entire engineering and technological chain, the project's most critical technical milestone,” he said.

During China's recent National Day holiday, the TRIDENT team completed a full battery of tests on the prototype detector string and successfully installed the unit in the deep sea, formally connecting it to the South China Sea observation network. The system is operating normally, the team reported.

Xu spent about a decade working on the IceCube Neutrino Observatory, an international project led by theoretical physicist Francis Halzen, who was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics earlier this week. Located in Antarctica, IceCube was built to detect high-energy neutrinos arriving from cosmic sources beyond our solar system.

Neutrinos are elementary particles and fundamental constituents of the universe. Because they interact so weakly with matter, they cannot ordinarily be detected directly. Scientists infer their properties by studying secondary particles generated when neutrinos interact with matter. Less than two years after IceCube's completion, the observatory detected extremely high-energy neutrinos originating beyond the Milky Way, helping establish neutrino astronomy as a new field of scientific research.

Xu began spearheading the development of TRIDENT, a next-generation high-energy neutrino telescope, in 2018. In 2021, the project team selected a site 3,500 meters beneath the sea in the Xisha waters of the South China Sea. The telescope, now under construction, is designed to achieve detection sensitivity more than 1,000 times greater than IceCube's.

“Seawater causes far less scattering than Antarctic glacial ice, which allows for a qualitative leap in the telescope's angular resolution,” Xu pointed out.

TRIDENT's first phase is intended as a pilot to demonstrate feasibility. It will deploy 10 detector strings, representing about one-tenth of IceCube's scale, and its main objective will be to validate the entire engineering and technological chain required to build and operate a deep-sea neutrino telescope in Chinese waters.

TRIDENT incorporates numerous technological innovations and design improvements over IceCube. The project is expected eventually to work in coordination with IceCube in Antarctica as part of a global neutrino-observation network, according to Xu.

“IceCube also will be upgraded in Antarctica to a second-generation facility,” Xu said. “We hope to establish a global neutrino-observation network that combines competition with complementarity.”

Editor: Tom Litting

data.title: China's Rino.ai Secures USD100 Million in Series C Funding for L4 Driving, Global Expansion
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 8 -- Rino.ai, a Chinese producer of unmanned delivery vehicles, has raised USD100 million in Series C funding to accelerate technology development and expand its operations.

The latest Series C2 financing brings Rino.ai's total Series C funding to USD100 million, following a Series C1 round completed in May for which the company did not disclose the amount raised. Last year, the firm secured nearly CNY500 million (USD74.6 million) through Series B and B+ funding rounds led by SF Holding.

The Series C2 round was led by Hidden Hill Capital, a private equity investment platform under global logistics giant GLP, with participation from state-backed investors in China's Hunan province, South Korea's Woori Financial Group, and Bozheng Capital Investment, an investment arm of Bohai Securities, according to a statement released today.

The Beijing-based company will use the proceeds of the Series C2 round to advance its Level 4 autonomous driving technology, which allows vehicles to operate without human intervention under specified conditions. It will also enhance its physical artificial intelligence capabilities and expand its urban delivery network.

Founded in 2019 by former Baidu autonomous driving team members Zhu Lei and Xia Tian, Rino.ai has partnered with express delivery giant SF Holding, national postal service provider China Post Group, e-commerce giant JD.Com, on-demand logistics platform Lalamove, and Alibaba Group Holding's instant retail arm Taobao Flash Shopping. The company has delivered more than 5,000 unmanned logistics vehicles and operates in over 200 Chinese cities.

With fresh funding, Rino.ai aims to expand alongside its partners. The startup will tap Singapore-headquartered GLP's global logistics infrastructure and warehousing assets to develop unmanned delivery services and accelerate commercial validation, while leveraging Woori Financial Group's cross-border resources to expand its autonomous driving operations overseas.

Rino.ai also intends to deepen industry partnerships and integrate its technology, products, operations, and broader ecosystem to strengthen its long-term competitiveness, it added.

Editor: Emmi Laine

data.title: China Merchants Energy Shipping Surges on USD2.8 Billion Deal for Africa’s Mega Iron Ore Project
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 8 -- Shares of China Merchants Energy Shipping surged today after its Hong Kong subsidiary secured a long-term iron ore shipping contract worth at least USD2.8 billion for Guinea’s Simandou project, expected to become Africa’s largest integrated mining and infrastructure development.

CMES [SHA: 601872], the shipping arm of state-owned conglomerate China Merchants Group, closed 9.3 percent elevated at CNY22.03 (USD3.30) after remaining near the 10 percent daily price increase limit for most of the trading session.

CMES's wholly owned subsidiary, Ming Wah Shipping, signed the 25-year transportation service agreement with a client holding shipping rights for iron ore produced at Simandou, located in West Africa, according to a recent announcement released by the leading Chinese crude oil and dry bulk shipping provider.

Under the agreement, Ming Wah will deploy six very large ore carriers (VLOCs) to transport iron ore from the project. The company did not disclose further details of the agreement or identify the client.

Previous filings by CMES show that although Simandou's northern and southern mining blocks are controlled by different entities, both have awarded the overall supply chain contracting rights for all iron ore exports to China Mineral Resources Group International Supply Chain, the trading and logistics arm of state-owned iron ore importer China Mineral Resources Group.

In July, CMES announced plans to invest up to CNY4.9 billion (USD682.1 million) to build six new-generation, energy-efficient and environmentally friendly VLOCs of 343,000 deadweight tons each, due for delivery between 2029 and 2030.

At the time, the company did not say what the vessels would be used for, only that they would serve long-term shipping agreements known as contracts of affreightment, under which shipping companies commit to carrying an agreed amount of cargo over a set period. The company said the contracts would help strengthen ties with major customers.

The Simandou project in southeastern Guinea is being developed in two parts. A consortium led by China Baowu Steel Group controls the northern blocks. The southern blocks are being developed by a joint venture led by Rio Tinto, with Aluminum Corporation of China among its major shareholders.

The project, a large open-pit mine for high-grade hematite iron ore, officially began operations at the end of last year, and production is ramping up. It has estimated reserves of about 4.4 billion tons, with an iron content of more than 65 percent, and is expected to produce 120 million tons a year once fully operational.

Editor: Emmi Laine

data.title: China’s JAC Motors Says It Is in Talks With Huawei, Stellantis, But No Deal Yet
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 8 -- JAC Motors has confirmed for the first time that the Chinese auto manufacturer is in discussions with tech giant Huawei Technologies and Dutch carmaker Stellantis about a potential cooperation. However, the scope and structure of any tie-up have yet to be determined and no legally binding agreement has been signed.

JAC Motors also said in the announcement made on Sept. 30 that, following an internal review and verification with its controlling shareholder, as of the date of the announcement, there were no major matters that should have been disclosed but have not been disclosed.

Reuters reported on Sept. 4, citing two sources, that Stellantis was in talks with Shenzhen-based Huawei and JAC Group over a long-term industrial cooperation involving its struggling luxury brand Maserati. Stellantis CEO Antonio Filosa told Italian business newspaper Milano Finanza that the talks were at an advanced stage and revolved around potentially using Huawei’s Harmony Intelligent Mobility platform for Maserati. The plan reportedly aims to start production ⁠of the first jointly developed vehicle by the end of next year.

The potential partnership could also include a dual-branding strategy, with a vehicle marketed under JAC’s Maextro luxury marque in China and under the Maserati brand in international markets.

But JAC Motors’ latest announcement did not confirm if the possible tie-up would involve Maserati, Maextro or any other specific model.

JAC Motors’ share price [SHA: 600418] plunged by the exchange-imposed limit of 10 percent at CNY24.72 (USD3.70) today. Between Sept. 28 and Sept. 30, the three days before the seven-day National Day holiday began, the Hefei-based firm’s share price rose sharply, with the cumulative deviation from the relevant market index exceeding 20 percent.

JAC Motors logged a net loss attributable to shareholders of CNY749 million (USD11.7 million) the first six months, according to its semi-annual financial report released on Aug. 20. Excluding non-recurring items and losses, its net loss was CNY991 million.

Hoofddorp-based Stellantis was formed in 2021 through the merger of Fiat Chrysler Automobiles and Peugeot Citroën Group. Its portfolio includes Maserati, Jeep, Peugeot, Fiat and other car brands.

Editor: Kim Taylor

data.title: AI PhD Holders From China’s Top Universities Enjoy Pay Boom
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 8 -- Salaries for PhD graduates in artificial intelligence from China’s elite universities are climbing, with compensation hitting several million Chinese yuan (millions of US dollars) and more, amid surging demand for talent in the field.

PhD holders from top labs at Peking University and Tsinghua University who join AI projects at big technology firms can earn multi-million yuan annual packages (cash, stocks, and options), one AI startup’s founder told Yicai, adding that some AI master’s degree graduates can also command daily remuneration in the thousands of yuan.

TikTok owner ByteDance, whose Beijing headquarters is less than 10 kilometers from Peking University, is a major draw for its graduates. Yang Ling, an assistant professor in the International Machine Learning Research Center at Peking University, said many of its postgraduates have interned at ByteDance.

Some Peking University PhD students have already taken deep dives into ByteDance’s research projects during their studies, Yang said. “Many interns hold important roles within ByteDance’s research teams and may even participate directly in model training,” he noted.

A top-flight researcher can save a company from much futile model training, Yang said, explaining the reason for the hefty salaries. A single experiment can cost several million to tens of millions of yuan, making high annual salaries well worth the investment, he pointed out.

The AI startup’s founder echoed that sentiment, saying that an annual salary of several million yuan looks reasonable as long as the hired expert can help the company’s AI projects make chip use more efficient.

“Large models represent the most valuable track right now, and professionals in this sector are the most valuable talent of this era,” the founder said.

“Many PhDs from Peking University and Tsinghua University now go straight to [large tech firms] to take on core tasks, directly replacing the previous generation of tech talent,” Yang stated.

But even this talented cohort could be replaced by even more capable people in a couple of years’ time, according to Yang, who expects the AI talent shortage to ease over the next five years. Universities will produce more AI graduates, and model developers will cultivate in-house talent pools, while industrial expansion may hit a ceiling, and demand for talent will not keep expanding at the current rapid pace.

Yang said the demand for AI talent will become sharply polarized. “Only the very top tier — those capable of delivering genuinely high-value outputs -- will remain critical. The importance of everyone else will decline,” he said.

Yang cited AI coding platforms as an example. They are making the work of junior programmers dispensable. “Codex can handle the tasks these people used to perform,” he said, referring to the AI coding platform developed by OpenAI.

This means universities must adapt to meet the challenge. “Peking University is changing, and other universities are following suit,” the startup’s founder said. “Higher education institutions must integrate with industry. Without such integration, they will struggle to secure research funding, and students will fail to gain practical knowledge.”

Editor: Tang Shihua

data.title: Shanghai Home Sales Rise Over National Day Holiday
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 8 -- Housing projects in Shanghai have seen an increase in viewings and sales after the city introduced new property market polices before the National Day holiday and potential buyers returned to the city toward the end of the week-long break, according to industry insiders.

“I’ve lost count of how many clients I’ve hosted at peak times,” Cao Xiao, a brand representative for a development in Shanghai’s Yangpu district, told Yicai. On the morning of Oct. 7, after spending nearly an hour walking a prospective buyer through the property, she immediately moved on to the next. “It was basically non-stop. My feet were swollen by the end of the day."

Scenes like this were repeated across Shanghai. A sales director at a project in Pudong New Area said many prospective buyers visited with their families over the holiday, a factor that accelerated their buying decisions.

As the first lowdensity residential development launch in the area in more than a decade, it attracted a large number of interested local buyers. During the combined Mid-Autumn Festival and National Day holiday period, the project had over 500 customer visits and secured new purchase commitments totaling CNY420 million (USD62.7 million).

In late August, the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development, the People's Bank of China, and other government bodies issued major policies to overhaul the age-worn model governing real estate development and sales. Among the changes, mortgage timelines were a top concern for prospective homebuyers.

At the end of last month, Shanghai released detailed regulations on the sale of completed homes, tightening presales management, raising sales thresholds, and strengthening the oversight of funds. Under the new rules, for newbuild projects granted presale permits on or after Aug. 28, homebuyers who have signed a contract and made down payment, are not required to begin repaying the loan’s principal and interest before the home's completion filing is finalized.

These detailed rules eliminated uncertainty, enabling clients to make faster decisions, according to industry insiders. For some first-time buyers with genuine housing needs, the current policy -- requiring only a down payment with no mortgage repayments for the subsequent two and a half years -- eases the financial burden and encourages leverage. Meanwhile, the new framework also enables well-heeled buyers looking to move higher up the market to acquire highquality property with less capital tiedup.

“Before the new policy, 70 percent to 80 percent of upgrade buyers would pay in full, but since the policy took effect, they have all opted for the 15 percent down payment," a seasoned property industry professional revealed. "For these clients, the potential appreciation of the capital they retain is certainly more attractive that the roughly 3 percent annual interest cost on a home loan.”

The new policy framework has also brought about a series of other changes. Shifts in developers' cost structures driven by the new policy have led some projects to pull discounts, while others have signaled price hikes for upcoming batches of units, said Lu Wenxi, a senior market analyst at Centaline Property. This has created a sense of urgency among prospective buyers who are viewing properties or negotiating deals, he said.

“As Shanghai's detailed implementation rules officially take effect, market anxiety is expected to gradually subside," Lu predicted. He expects the market to return to normal transaction levels this month, with sales activity outside of the Outer Ring Road likely to maintain its current momentum.

Editor: Tom Litting

data.title: Chinese EV Giant BYD Enters Namibian Market in Global Expansion Drive
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 7 -- Chinese automaker BYD has officially launched its new energy vehicle brand in Namibia, expanding its presence in the African market.

Namibian automotive distributor Pupkewitz Motors announced yesterday that it will represent BYD in the country, with the brand to be offered through retail outlets in Windhoek, Walvis Bay and Ongwediva.

"Our ambition is not simply to introduce new vehicles to the market, but to create an experience around new energy mobility that is relevant to Namibian customers. We look forward to building awareness, educating consumers and allowing customers to experience BYD for themselves," said Nico Pieters, a franchise executive at Pupkewitz Motors, in a statement.

Models being introduced to the Namibian market include the BYD Dolphin, BYD Dolphin Surf, BYD Sealion 5, BYD Sealion 6, BYD Shark 6, BYD Sealion 7 and BYD Seal Performance.

"The range allows Namibian customers to explore different forms of electrified mobility while experiencing the technology, comfort and features associated with the BYD brand," Pieters said.

He said the launch comes as energy efficiency, sustainability and the future of transportation gain increasing attention globally.

"BYD's global focus on new energy technologies places the brand at the forefront of this changing automotive landscape, while its entry into Namibia provides local motorists with greater access to alternative vehicle technologies," he added.

With the official launch of BYD, Pupkewitz Motors is expanding its portfolio to include a global new energy vehicle brand, reinforcing its commitment to providing Namibian customers with greater choice as mobility evolves.

In September, economic and market indicators from Namibian firm IJG Securities, showed that Chinese brands are steadily gaining popularity in Namibia. Haval, Jetour and Chery accounted for 5.9 percent, 5.8 percent and 2.3 percent, respectively, of the Namibian passenger vehicle market.

Editor: Dou Shicong
